# MyoSuite Native Muscle-Excitation Replay (Provisional)

## Scope

This note specifies the MyoSuite open-loop consumer of the versioned Tools T01
`experiment-replay/1.0.0` bundle. Its implementation is
`src/engines/physics_engines/myosuite/python/native_excitation_replay.py` and
its F09 integration is `src/engines/feedback_native_execution.py`. It is an
execution adapter, not a new bundle schema, scoring rule, capability registry,
or qualification authority.

The adapter currently exercises a pinned MyoSuite 3.0.0 and MuJoCo 3.6.0
runtime. It retains the F01 model inventory identity separately from the T01
native model/provider identity and F06 execution binding. A bundle can run only
when an explicit registration binds those identities, ordered channels,
complete state schema, input schema, and loaded model. A runtime smoke using
MyoSuite's built-in elbow task does not register or qualify a golfer model.

## Applied Input and Time

Let \(u_k\) denote the ordered normalized muscle-excitation vector at the
simulation-relative controller sample \(t_k\). The frozen T01 input is the
post-mapping value written directly to MuJoCo actuator controls:

\[
  \texttt{data.ctrl}(t) = u_k,
  \qquad t_k \le t < t_{k+1},
  \qquad t_{k+1}-t_k = n_f h,
\]

where \(h\) is the native MuJoCo integration step and \(n_f\) is the pinned
MyoSuite `frame_skip`. The input uses dimensionless unit `1`, zero-order hold,
and a terminal sentinel that repeats the final applied sample. The actual
native controls are read back before stepping and must equal \(u_k\); native
actuator limits are checked without clipping or modifying the frozen input.

The Gym action vector is a different boundary. In the pinned environment,
MyoSuite's action handling transforms normalized Gym commands before setting
muscle controls. Therefore a `[-1, 1]` command cannot be labeled muscle
excitation, and the adapter does not infer controls by inverting the wrapper
transform. No inverse is defined at activation endpoints, and no synthetic
endpoint values are introduced.

The plant is advanced using the registered model's native MuJoCo step for the
declared frame skip. The adapter does not call Gym `step`; consequently task
observations, rewards, environment termination, task resets, and task RNG are
outside this run. The policy and provider identity declare this direct-plant,
fixed-horizon path and bind solver, integrator, source/loaded model, runtime,
wrapper chain, actuator mapping, time step, and frame skip.

## Complete Initialization and Output

The full initial-state payload contains, in fixed order:

- native `qpos` and `qvel`, whose dimensions remain independent;
- MyoSuite muscle activation and the current native actuator controls;
- MuJoCo `mjSTATE_INTEGRATION`, including its numerical warm-start state; and
- supported wrapper state: TimeLimit elapsed steps, order-enforcement reset
  flag, passive-checker flags, and the MyoSuite instability-termination flag.

For the pinned MuJoCo 3.6 runtime, `mjSTATE_INTEGRATION` combines full physics,
user state, and warm-start state. It therefore includes native time,
configuration/velocity/activation/history, controls and applied loads,
constraint activation, mocap state, user data, and solver warm-start state;
MuJoCo plugin state is separately rejected by this adapter. See the
[MuJoCo 3.6 state API](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/3.6.0/APIreference/APItypes.html).
This native payload is distinct from Gym wrapper state and any task RNG.

State-schema identity and the actual payload digest are both checked. Wrapper
state is frozen and preserved because Gym stepping is not part of this policy;
it does not stand in for task RNG state or establish wrapper behavior during a
Gym episode. The returned trajectory includes native configuration/velocity,
activation, controls, integration state, wrapper-state snapshot, exact applied
input samples, and the T01 input/policy digests. It contains no marker positions
or observation score.

The loader fails closed if the registered model source changes during load,
the wrapper chain differs, a control stage or plugin is present, muscle
activation state does not map one-to-one to the declared actuators, a channel
or clock differs, state restoration changes the frozen payload, or actual
control readback does not match the bundle. Only the explicitly supported
control readback does not match the bundle. It also rejects process-global
MuJoCo callbacks before construction and around native stepping/forward
evaluation, checks that post-step `data.time` matches the frozen clock, rejects
nonfinite physical or integration state, and verifies that `mj_forward` leaves
the observed clock unchanged. Output timestamps are observed native times, not
a copy of requested timestamps. Only the explicitly supported wrapper
attributes are restored. A future environment with additional mutable state
requires a separately versioned state and policy contract.

## Evidence and Limitations

The independent contract suite tests wrong drive-mode and policy rejection,
identity binding, explicit F09 dispatch, and continued retention of all
required rows and six engines. A separate actual-runtime smoke test builds a
frozen excitation bundle, runs MyoSuite 3.0.0/MuJoCo 3.6.0, and verifies exact
control readback, full-horizon state output, and digest preservation. This
fixture is an installed public elbow task, not private capture data or a
production golf model.

The callback-ownership and observed-clock checks were added after the retained
DeskComputer runtime execution. Their synthetic MuJoCo regressions pass in the
local environment, but this exact source revision has not yet been rerun under
the pinned MyoSuite 3.0.0/MuJoCo 3.6.0 runtime. The earlier native result applies
only to the source bytes used by its disposable overlay; it is not evidence for
the newer revision.

The task-owned MyoSuite 3.0.0 distribution metadata reports
`License-Expression: Apache-2.0`; the upstream [MyoSuite source
repository](https://github.com/MyoHub/myosuite) publishes that license. The
[MyoSuite 3.0.0 release page](https://pypi.org/project/MyoSuite/3.0.0/)
documents the pinned `myo-sim==0.2.3` model package used by this runtime. The
installed `myo-sim` metadata reports `License: Apache 2.0`; its [0.2.3 PyPI
release](https://pypi.org/project/myo-sim/0.2.3/) identifies the packaged
musculoskeletal model library. This is provenance for the public test
environment only; no model or license claim is made for the required golf
variants or any capture data.

F01's `myosuite/driver` and `myosuite/iron` remain required, supported at the
package-surface level, availability unknown, and qualification unqualified
until each has an explicit reviewed source/provider/model binding and required
native acceptance evidence. MuJoCo 3.8 torque evidence is not MyoSuite
excitation evidence. No physiology tolerance, observation score, reset count,
production capability, or cross-engine equivalence is inferred by this
adapter. All other engine and model rows remain in the denominator.

The generic MyoSuite engine's handling of legacy Gym four-value step results
is outside this provider because it never calls `env.step`. That wrapper path
needs its own regression test and issue if a legacy environment is supported;
it is not silently certified by this native replay.

## Direct Model-Path Replay Kernel

The F09g direct replay kernel in
`src/engines/physics_engines/myosuite/python/native_direct_model_replay.py`
reuses the T01 `ACTUATOR_COMMAND` bundle with an inspected, source-bound native
model factory. The factory receives the original model path so relative MJCF
includes and mesh/texture paths retain their declared resource root. The
kernel binds the caller-declared resource set, compiled actuator laws/channel
order, full numerical state and contact/solver/step policy. It restores full
integration state, checks the caller-declared resource files, and rejects
callbacks, plugins, wrappers, warnings, resets and nonfinite or off-clock
output. It calls only native MuJoCo stepping and forward evaluation. It does
not convert the input into torque or Gym actions, call environment `step`, or
create a qualification receipt. A bounded MuJoCo 3.8.0 disk-MJCF audit follows
tested include resolution and native MjSpec mesh/texture/cube-face metadata;
each discovered source and asset must be hash-matched in the supplied
inventory before the preflight compiled MJB is checked against the expected
loaded-model identity. This admits the current XML, STL/MSH and PNG route only.

The public driver and iron command fixtures replayed exactly against all saved
native state samples on MuJoCo 3.8.0. Those runs used the underlying MuJoCo XML
loader and do not establish official MyoSuite `MujocoEnv` constructor
compatibility or MyoSuite 3.6 execution. No golfer production binding is
registered by the direct kernel; the required MyoSuite driver/iron rows and
all six engine variants stay in the denominator. The reviewed execution
boundary and opt-in validation command are recorded in
`docs/development/feedback_controls/F09G-DIRECT-MODEL-REPLAY.md`.
The kernel accepts only `engine_id="mujoco"`; all other IDs fail before factory
invocation. The source admission is version- and loader-specific, not a general
MJCF closure parser: it rejects absolute/URI paths, URDF, VFS, `strippath`,
hfields, skins, attach/flexcomp, plugins, content-type overrides and other
unreviewed file loaders before native parsing. The official MyoSuite path
remains closed until its exact supported SDK constructor and runtime are
inspected and pinned. The bounded direct MuJoCo evidence does not qualify that
SDK route or the production capture models.

An additional opt-in diagnostic uses the pinned public MyoSim `arm/myoarm.xml`
donor under MuJoCo 3.8.0. It compiles 63 native muscle/tendon actuators and
replays a short unitless `ACTUATOR_COMMAND` pulse exactly from full integration
state. This is a muscle-only upper-limb candidate, not a golfer model or an
official MyoSuite runtime result. Its unmodified default state has two
penetrating contacts and a large humerus/thorax contact force, so this run does
not establish an admissible equilibrium or capture result. The model's
`na=63` activation states also expose why F05's current two-motor torque
tangent derivative cannot be reused: a muscle tangent state must include
activation dynamics in addition to manifold configuration and velocity. The
source, hashes, command, and exact limits are recorded in
`docs/development/feedback_controls/F09G-MYOARM-DIAGNOSTIC.md`. An exploratory
one-step centered finite difference produced finite `139 x 139` state and
`139 x 63` input matrices. The apparent derivative blow-up is traced to the
stock `md3_flexion` coordinate starting exactly at its lower joint limit:
central perturbations place one trial inside and the other outside the
compiled range. A diagnostic in-memory copy with only joint limits disabled
stabilizes this derivative; disabling equality constraints or contacts alone
does not. Muscle force, tendon length and estimated moment arms vary smoothly,
while the generalized constraint force changes from zero to about `0.412 N`.
This isolates a derivative problem at a nonsmooth limit boundary; it does not
qualify the altered model or the stock state for control. The full audit
script and source-hashed receipt are in
`docs/development/feedback_controls/f09g_myoarm_fd_audit.py.txt` and
`docs/development/feedback_controls/F09G-MYOARM-FD-AUDIT-MJ38.json`.
The bounded source/resource admission extension is tracked in F09h (#11950); see
`docs/development/feedback_controls/F09H-NATIVE-RESOURCE-CLOSURE.md`.
